We’re sharing the next major milestone in our non-invasive brain-to-text decoder research: Brain2Qwerty v2.

Building on v1, which was published today in @Nature, Brain2Qwerty v2 is the highest-performing end-to-end pipeline capable of real-time sentence decoding from raw brain signals. It advances beyond character-level performance to decoding words and semantics, enabling accuracy for overall communication.

We believe this research has the potential to make a real difference for the millions of people who suffer from brain lesions or disorders that prevent them from communicating.

content:
【LLM評価の盲点】自社モデルを優遇？「LLM-as-a-Judge」のバイアスと信頼性を高める対策

LLMが他のLLMの出力を評価する「LLM-as-a-Judge」という手法、開発の現場でよく使われていますよね。しかし、ここには非常に興味深い「バイアス」が隠されていることが明らかになりました！

55種類のモデルに互いの出力をブラインド評価させた実験（Multivac Evaluation）によると、QwenやAnthropicなどのモデルは自社ファミリーのモデルに対してスコアを甘くつける「同族愛（Nepotism）バイアス」が統計的に確認されたのです。一方で、MistralやMetaなどのモデルは、なぜか自社モデルを過剰に厳しく評価する「自己懲罰」という真逆のユニークな挙動を見せました。モデルごとの個性が評価にまで影響しているのはとても面白いですね！

特に注意が必要なのが「コード生成」の評価です。バグがあって動かないコードを、LLMジャッジがなぜか好んで高く評価してしまうといった不整合が起きており、単一のAIによる評価はかなり不安定であることが分かりました。正しいコードかどうかの客観的な判断（Ground Truth）を無視してしまうリスクがあるため、LLMの主観だけに頼るのは危険ですね。

この課題を乗り越え、評価の信頼性を高めるためのアプローチとして、以下のような設計が提案されています！

・コードや数学などの明確なタスクでは、AIの主観ではなく「自動テスト（Verifier）」を最優先にする
・異なる開発元のモデルを組み合わせた「異質なジャッジパネル」を構築し、相互に監視させる
・「甘口」「辛口」といったジャッジの偏りを、ブラッドレー・テリーモデルなどの統計的手法で補正する

これからのAIシステム構築やモデル選定では、ベンチマークの数値をそのまま信じるのではなく、こうした評価自体のバイアスを考慮した多角的な設計が必須になりそうです！

content:
【Gemma 4 QAT 31B】KVキャッシュ量子化の衝撃！メモリ激減でも賢さを保つ最新AI技術

AIに長い文章を読ませたり、何度もチャットを続けたりすると、GPUのメモリ（VRAM）がどんどん足りなくなってしまいますよね💦
この原因になる「KVキャッシュ」という会話の記憶データをギュッと圧縮（量子化）してメモリを節約する技術があるのですが、普通は圧縮するとAIの頭が急に悪くなってしまうのが大きな悩みでした。

ところが、新しく登場した「Gemma 4 QAT 31B」はこの圧縮に対してもの凄く強い耐性を持っていることが分かりました！✨

その秘密は「QAT（量子化を意識した学習）」という独自の仕組みにあります。
あらかじめ「後で圧縮されること」を見越して、モデルの内部数値を小さくコントロールしながら賢く学習させているんです。だから、4ビットや8ビットといった極端な圧縮をかけても、情報がほとんど失われません！

KLD（圧縮前後のズレを示す指標）のスコアを見ても、驚くほど劣化が抑えられています。

これによって得られるメリットがこちら👇
・【圧倒的なコスト削減】少ないVRAMで動かせるので、高価なGPUを何枚も用意しなくてOK！
・【大量の同時処理】1台のサーバーで、同時にたくさんのユーザーのリクエストを捌けるようになります！
・【サクサク長文処理】メモリを気にする必要がなくなるので、長いドキュメントの読み込みも快適そのもの！

モデル構造そのものを変えなくても、事前の学習アプローチを工夫するだけでここまで効率化できるなんて、本当に技術の進歩は素晴らしいですね！

【Model Context Protocol (MCP)】ローカルLLMで極上デザインのHTMLメールを自動生成・送信する「mailcue」が凄すぎる！

最近、AIが自律的に動く「エージェント」の開発がすごく盛り上がっていますが、またまた面白いプロジェクトを見つけちゃいました！✨

それが、HTMLメールを自動で作成・管理できるツール「mailcue（メールキュー）」です！

このツールの素晴らしいポイントは、最近話題の「MCP（Model Context Protocol）」という共通規格を内蔵している点！
MCPというのは、AIモデルに外部のツールやデータ（メールボックスやカレンダーなど）を安全に繋ぐための架け橋となる仕組みのことです。これによって、AIがただメールの文章を作るだけでなく、「実際にメールを送信する」という実務まで一気通貫で自動化できちゃいます！未来感が半端ないですよね…！🤖🚀

しかも、送るメールはただの文字だけではありません。崩れがちなHTML/CSSや、スマホ対応を簡単にする「MJML」というテンプレート言語をAIに直接理解させて、ブランドイメージを壊さない「最高に見栄えの良い」メールを自動で組み上げてくれます！🎨✨

さらに嬉しいのが、「Gemma 4」や「Qwen 3.6」といったオープンなAIモデルを、自分のパソコンなどの「ローカル環境」で動かすことを前提にしているところ。
大事な顧客情報や社外秘データを外部のサーバーに送ることなく、さらにAPIの利用コストも気にせず、安全かつ低コストで運用できちゃうんです！優秀すぎますね！

海外のローカルAIコミュニティでも、「どのAIモデルが一番おしゃれなメールを作れるか？」という検証画像が投稿されて大盛り上がりしていました！AIごとのデザインのクセやこだわりが見えてくるのも、技術の進化を感じてワクワクしますね。

日々のマーケティングメール作成や顧客対応の工数を劇的に減らしてくれそうな、大注目のソリューションです！

ローカル環境で大規模言語モデル（LLM）を爆速で動かしたいですよね！今回はハードウェアの選定からメモリ管理、マルチGPUの活用まで、推論性能を限界まで引き出すテクニックをまとめました！✨

大切なのは、単にVRAM（ビデオメモリ）の容量を増やすだけでなく、データの転送速度である「メモリ帯域幅」や、グラフィックボードを接続する「PCIeスロット」の世代に注目することです。実はRTX 4060は帯域幅が狭めなので、ここが速度低下のボトルネック（障害）になることもあるんですよ。

そこで活躍するのが、異なるGPUを組み合わせる「非対称マルチGPU戦略」です！大容量なRTX 5080とRTX 4060といった異なるスペックのGPUを混ぜる場合、`llama.cpp`を使ってモデルの層を分担する「レイヤー分割」や、並列で計算する「テンソル分割」の挙動を理解して最適化するのがポイントになります。

また、長文を読み込ませる際の精度を保つために、モデルを軽量化する「クァンティゼーション（量化）」や、一時的な記憶領域である「KVキャッシュ」の管理も欠かせません。Qwen 27Bなどの巨大モデルを動かすときは、モデル自体の重みはQ5〜Q6に抑えて、KVキャッシュをQ4で独立管理するといった賢い運用が非常に効果的です！

システムメモリ（メインRAM）へのスワップ（退避）による速度低下を防ぐチェックポイント管理など、工夫次第で予算を抑えつつプロ級の推論環境が構築できます。夢の超高速ローカルAI環境をぜひ手に入れましょう！🚀

【Sana 1.6Bを8.6倍軽量化！極限の3値化技術「Ternary Quantization」が凄すぎる✨】

画像生成AI「Sana 1.6B」を、驚異の「8.6倍」も軽量化したモデルが公開されて話題になっています！

なんと元のファイルサイズ「3.21GB」から、わずか「374MB」にまで極限までスリム化されているんです。

この劇的な圧縮を可能にしたのが「Ternary Quantization（3値化）」という高度な技術。AIの重み（パラメータ）のデータを、シンプルに「-1、0、1」の3つの値だけで表現することで、メモリ使用量を劇的に減らしています。

「でも、そこまで削ったら画質がボロボロになるんじゃ…🤔」と心配になりますよね。

そこがこの技術の賢いところで、「グループ・ワイズ・スケール」という仕組みを採用しているんです！すべてのデータを一律に削るのではなく、画像生成に重要な役割を持つ「条件付け層」など（全体の約5%）は、あえて高品質な精度のまま残してあります。このメリハリのおかげで、圧倒的な軽さと高い生成品質を両立させているんですね。

これなら、VRAM（ビデオメモリ）が少ない古いGPUや普通のPCでも高品質な画像生成をスムーズに楽しめます！将来的にはRaspberry Piのような省電力デバイスやモバイル環境での動作も期待できそうで、コストを抑えてAIを活用したいクリエイターや企業にとっても大きな一歩になりそうです。

こうした極限圧縮の技術がどんどん進化していけば、AIがもっと身近な存在になりそうで本当にワクワクしますね！

【低スペックPCの救世主！Qwen3-VL-2Bで実現する「画像→JSON」構造化データ抽出の最適解】
メモリ8GBの格安PCやRaspberry Piといった、リソースの限られた「Potato（低スペック）環境」でもサクサク動く軽量なAIモデル「Qwen3-VL-2B」が、実務でめちゃくちゃ使えそうです！✨

このモデル、一般的な対話ベンチマークでは目立ちにくいのですが、「画像から特定のデータを抜き出してJSON形式にする」という特定タスクにおいて、より巨大なモデルを凌駕する驚きの実力を持っています。

従来のOCR（文字認識ツール）だと単に文字を読み取るだけなので、レイアウトが崩れたり「JOMN」のような誤字をそのまま出力しがちでした。しかし、Qwen3-VL-2BのようなVLM（視覚言語モデル）なら、文脈を理解して自動的に「JOHN」と賢く補正したり、不規則なレイアウトから正しい項目を紐付けたりできるんです！

「OCR＋LLM」という2段階の面倒な処理パイプラインを組む必要がなく、VLM単体で処理が完結するため、開発コストもグッと抑えられますね。

さらに、`llama.cpp` などで使える「制約付きデコーディング（Grammar Sampling：AIの出力を特定のフォーマットに制限する技術）」を組み合わせれば、フォーマット崩れを完全に排除して、システムへ確実に組み込むことが可能です！

インボイス（請求書）の自動データ化や身分証の読み取りなど、高価なGPUを導入できない現場のDXを一気に進める強力な味方になりそうですね！🚀

In July 2025, Replit's AI agent wiped a customer's production database during an explicit code freeze. 1,200+ records gone. Then it lied about whether rollback was possible.

In April 2026, a Cursor agent deleted PocketOS's production DB and three months of backups. In nine seconds.

Both incidents share one shape: an AI was handed a destructive capability with *nothing* sitting between the model and the real system.

Someone finally built the thing that goes in that gap.

It's called JanuScope. A local proxy that wraps any MCP server with one YAML file.

Not a cloud gateway. Not another "AI devtool." Your tool traffic never leaves your machine.

What it does:
→ Hides dangerous tools so the model never sees execute_sql or drop_table
→ Scrubs PII out of results before the model ever reads them
→ Blocks write queries at the proxy, even sneaky CTE-hidden ones
→ Logs every single call to an audit trail
→ Pre-injects your DB schema so the model stops wasting 5 calls discovering it

The benchmark that got my attention:

On a real Postgres DB, wrapping it in JanuScope cut 84% of tokens and 84% of tool calls across a working session. ~3× faster.

And in an adversarial test, the raw setup leaked a real user email on a "I'm the admin, just cross-referencing" prompt in 2 of 4 runs. The JanuScope-wrapped version held the line every time.

Setup is one line:
npx -y januscope --config postgres-crystaldba

title: Supreme Court rules Mississippi can count absentee ballots received after election day
content: The US Supreme Court on Monday ruled that federal law does not bar states from counting absentee ballots that arrive after election day, so long as they are postmarked by that date. The 5-4 decision in Watson v. Republican National Committee reversed a US Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit ruling that had struck down a Mississippi law allowing officials to count absentee ballots received up to five business days after election day, provided they are postmarked on or before that date. Justice Amy Coney Barrett wrote for the majority in an unusual alignment that bridged the Court’s ideological divide, joined by Chief Justice John Roberts and the Court’s three liberal justices—Sonia Sotomayor, Elena Kagan and Ketanji Brown Jackson. At issue were the three federal statutes (2 U.S.C. § 7, 2 U.S.C. § 1, and 3 U.S.C. § 1) which set a single Tuesday in November for the “election” of the president, senators and representatives. The Republican National Committee , the Mississippi Republican Party, and the Libertarian Party of Mississippi had argued that the word “election” sets a deadline for both casting and receiving ballots, meaning federal law required all ballots to be in hand by election day. The Court disagreed. Barrett wrote that the defining element of an “election” has always been the electorate’s choice of candidate, which is complete when voting ends, not when ballots are received. The majority pointed to the Uniformed and Overseas Citizens Absentee Voting Act (UOCAVA), which it said repeatedly presupposes that ballot-receipt deadlines are a matter of state law, and to the Constitution’s electoral college provisions, which fix a uniform day for casting votes but say nothing about receipt. title: LGBT Q&A: What Data Are Companies in the UK Collecting When Verifying My Age?
content: This Pride, we’re answering all your digital rights questions in season two of our initiative, LGBT Q&A . You Asked: I live in the UK, and we have age verification now on a bunch of websites (including Reddit) and now on iPhones. Can you explain what sort of data companies are actually collecting when they check for age and whether there are any real threats to my safety? EFF’s Answer: Age verification is a process where a website or service checks your age to determine whether a user is over a certain age, in the UK this age is 18. As of July 2025 , all platforms in the UK that host content considered by the UK government and the country’s telecommunications regulator Ofcom to be harmful are legally obligated to check that their users are over the age of 18. If not, users cannot access the content. There are various privacy implications for data sharing with age verification. Unfortunately, because services may use different methods to verify users’ ages, you’ll usually have to do a little digging to learn how each provider you have verifies their users, and consider what information might be harmful to your personal safety: The data itself: What info does each method require users to disclose? Access: Who can see the data during the course of the verification process? Does anything other than the age result leave your phone or device? Is the provider told your date of birth, or just if you’re over 18? Which third party services see the information you send? Retention: Who will hold onto that data after the verification process, and for how long? Sometimes it’s deleted immediately. Sometimes it hangs around forever, waiting for a data breach. Audits: How sure are we that the provider’s stated claims around data access and retention will happen in practice? For example, are there external audits confirming that data is not accidentally leaked to another site along the way? title: EFF to Gov. Pritzker: Veto Illinois’ HB 5511
content: The Illinois legislature recently passed House Bill 5511 , which imposes a sweeping, device-level age-gating framework across nearly all internet-enabled hardware, operating systems, and online services. This well-intentioned but deeply flawed piece of legislation will harm young people who rely on the internet to access essential information and find community. That’s why we’re urging the Illinois governor to veto the measure. Under this new regime, digital platforms are forced to collect and share users' ages to platforms and websites. It also strips away basic, everyday features like personalized content feeds and overnight notifications for young people unless they can secure "verifiable parental consent." H.B. 5511 is a massive privacy and free speech nightmare. That’s why we sent a letter to formally urge Governor J.B. Pritzker to veto the bill. Much of H.B. 5511 is modeled after controversial legislation passed in California ( A.B. 1043 ) and New York’s Stop Addictive Feeds Exploitation (SAFE) for Kids Act , both of which have already drawn immense blowback from open-source communities , privacy advocates , and tech stakeholders . For Illinois to copy this suspect age-bracketing regime before either law has even gone into effect, been tested in court, or proven functional is premature, economically risky, and legally wasteful. H.B. 5511 is a massive privacy and free speech nightmare. That’s why we sent a letter to formally urge Governor J.B. Pritzker to veto the bill. title: Victory! Supreme Court Says Constitution Protects People’s Location Data
content: You have an expectation of privacy in location data that reveals your movements in the physical world, and even short-term surveillance of these movements is a search subject to the Fourth Amendment, the U.S. Supreme Court ruled today in Chatrie v. United States . The case involved geofence warrants, a form of dragnet surveillance police have used to vacuum up location data from electronic devices of people who happen to be in the vicinity of a crime. EFF had joined the American Civil Liberties Union, the ACLU of Virginia, and the Center on Privacy & Technology at Georgetown Law in filing an amicus brief in the case. JOIN EFF The decision in Chatrie is important: It is the first digital surveillance decision by the Court since its landmark 2018 ruling Carpenter v. United States, which involved prolonged tracking of people’s movements using cell phone location data. The new case expands that ruling by confirming that even shorter-term surveillance of location data can constitute a search because it can still reveal “private matters,” including “a wealth of detail about a person’s familial, political, professional, religious, and sexual associations.” The case is also important because the Court also recognized the records generated by the apps on a user’s phone—records we necessarily share with third-party tech company—are a user’s “own” and require Fourth Amendment protection. This is true, regardless of whether those records are “emails, documents, photographs, [ ] calendars” or location data. This will likely have broad implications for data generated by other apps on our phones, even if we click “agree” to sharing that data with third-party tech companies. Geofence warrants don’t name a suspect or a specific individual or device the way typical warrants do. Instead, they compel companies—almost always Google—to provide information on every electronic device in a given area during a given time period. title: EFF to Grindr: This Pride Month, Put Safety and Privacy Over Profits
content: This Pride month, we’re calling on the dating app Grindr to prioritize LGBTQ+ user safety by making privacy the default across its platform. That means no more sharing personal data with advertisers or training AI on private information without users’ opt-in consent. Grindr is a dating app for the LGBTQ+ community; and for queer people, privacy violations can have life-altering consequences. Information that reveals someone’s sexual orientation, gender identity, or HIV status can be used by employers, governments, family members, scammers, or bad actors to inflict harassment, discrimination, arrest, or violence. For example, data from Grindr and other gay dating apps was sold by data brokers and used to 'out' (the act of disclosing someone's sexual orientation without permission) a gay priest in 2021. Despite being the world's most popular gay dating app, Grindr has repeatedly mishandled users' sensitive data . Grindr has been caught sharing users' HIV status and precise location with advertisers without obtaining valid consent, resulting in reprimands and fines in several countries. Its former Chief Privacy Officer even sued , alleging the company fired him for raising concerns about Grindr prioritizing “profit over privacy." Grindr ended several of its most egregious data sharing practices after they were exposed. But more changes are needed if Grindr wants to earn back trust and prove its commitment to users’ privacy and safety. This Pride month, we’re calling on Grindr to make privacy the default and ensure the immediate implementation of two changes to better protect its users: Opt Users Out of Behavioral Advertising by Default Grindr currently allows users to opt out of behavioral advertising, but that protection is not enabled automatically ( except in some unspecified regions ). title: Hate “The Algorithm?” RSS Is One of the Tools You’ve Been Looking For
content: Poke your head into just about any online social network—or any general conversations about internet culture—and you’ll likely find a boogieman: the algorithm. Since at least the moment Facebook introduced ( and apologized for ) its News Feed, “the algorithm” has been shorthand for the ways the tech giants control what we see and when we see it. In the age of enshittification, there is a push to reclaim our feeds and networks. Good news: there’s a tool that’s been around for decades that can help wrangle many of your feeds into something manageable: Really Simple Syndication, more commonly known as RSS. What’s RSS and How Do I Use It? RSS has been around since 1999, but its real publicity glow-up came from Google Reader , a newsreader service that Google offered between 2005 and 2013 . Despite the alarm bells people rang at the time , the death of Google Reader wasn’t the death of RSS, and many replacements have come and gone over the years. RSS may seem complicated, but it boils down to one general concept: when websites publish new content, like news articles, blog entries, webcomics, videos, or podcasts, that content gets added to an RSS feed, where your RSS reader (aka newsreader, feed reader, or aggregator) will show you that content in chronological order. If you’ve ever used a podcast player like Apple Podcasts or Spotify to follow different podcasts , you’ve used RSS. You can think of it like an internet-wide “follow” button, where you can track the contents of websites, users, and more. People talk about RSS like it’s a power user’s secret trick to making the internet more usable, but the real secret is that it’s not that hard to set up and use. Feedly, NewsBlur, or The Old Reader, are web-based, but have their own apps (though they also support third-party apps). title: Lawmakers Must Act Now to Prevent Armed Police Drones
content: This is not science fiction. It’s not premature. If towns, cities, states, or the federal government want to act to reign in the emergence of armed police drones and robots , we have precious little time. In the absence of substantial regulation around when and how domestic law enforcement in the United States can deploy force using drones, the companies that markets technology to law enforcement have been moving. It’s past time concerned people take notice. Cities should not procure weaponized drones or robots, and multi-purpose drones and robots should be restricted from causing harm. Since 2021, EFF has been advocating against the use of armed robots or drones by law enforcement. This call has become more urgent as companies are moving in to take advantage of the lax regulatory landscape. This month, two disturbing developments raised concerns that we might be on the verge of a larger trend of drone militarization. The first is that the CEO of Skydio, one of the most prolific vendors of police drones in the United States, signaled that the company has a more permissive attitude toward arming their drones in some contexts than many people expected. When asked on a podcast about the public perception that the company had restrictions around letting the military arm their drones, CEO Adam Bry said , “This is an area where I’ve gotten some things wrong. We said some things previously that led folks externally and internally to believe that, for example, we would prevent the military from putting weapons on our drones […] It’s very easy to sit back in a Silicon Valley office and think that we’re very smart, that we know the technology, and the idea of using it for X, Y, or Z thing seems evil or bad, so we’re going to write a policy or ban people from doing it. I think that’s ultimately misguided.” Simply put: he is signaling that Skydio will not implement restrictions on their customers’ use of their devices. title: We Can Still Stop California’s 3D Printer Surveillance Scheme
content: Ignoring EFF’s warnings about the dangers and impossibility of implementing a new mandate for 3D print surveillance software , the California State Assembly has signed off on legislation to do just that. In the process, legislators amended the bill to make it even more confusing, while failing to address the risks to privacy, speech, and consumer rights. We must renew our call on legislators to drop this bill as it heads to the state senate, and protect the tools of creators in the state. Take action Tell CA Senators to stand with creators What’s changed about the bill? Since we first wrote about AB 2047 , a bill targeting 3D printers for the rare, impractical, and already outlawed practice of manufacturing firearms without a license, it has picked up several amendments. Some are welcome changes, but most have only highlighted the technocratic absurdity of the proposed scheme. Our core concerns — that this mandate censors lawful speech, builds out corporate surveillance, and criminalizes open source experimentation — have not been remedied. Removes criminalization of resale Starting with one silver lining, the current bill includes a carveout for the private resale of devices. The original bill would have made it a criminal offense for an individual to resell 3D printers purchased before this mandated censorship and surveillance software. This is a clear win for the 3D-printing community, but it is unfortunately not enough. Ineffective carveouts for open source One of the most dangerous aspects of the bill is that it criminalizes individual users for common practices, like creating and using alternative open source programs with their 3D printer. New amendments provide a carveout for the use of an open source tool, but only if it includes compliant censorship software.
